findings.title: Security advisories: multiple vulnerabilities in Regexp and String case conversion
findings.summary_md: Ruby's advisory lists seven memory-safety flaws in the regular expression engine and string case conversion, and says proof-of-concept code shows that some can trigger remote code execution. It tracks the flaws as GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5, GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x, GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px, GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r, GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w, GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4 and GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h because CVE identifiers had been requested but not assigned. Affected versions are 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 through 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 through 4.0.9; the fixes are 3.3.14, 3.4.13 and 4.0.10, while Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life.

findings.title: Heap buffer overflow in case conversion of strings · Advisory · ruby/ruby
findings.summary_md: The GitHub advisory for GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5 describes a one-byte heap buffer overflow in Ruby's string case conversion that may allow remote code execution when a crafted string is case-converted. It lists affected versions up to 3.3.13, 3.4.0 through 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, with patches in 3.3.14, 3.4.13 and 4.0.10. The advisory thanks Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics and Anthropic for reporting the issue.

findings.title: Ruby: multiple vulnerabilities in Regexp and String case conversion
findings.summary_md: Alan Coopersmith reposted Ruby's advisory to oss-sec, quoting the seven memory-safety flaws and the maintainers' statement that proof-of-concept exploits can trigger remote code execution in some scenarios. The message lists all seven GHSA identifiers, the affected ranges of 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 through 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, and the fixed releases 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14. It adds no exploitation telemetry of its own.

findings.title: Ruby ships fixes for regexp and string bugs, some with RCE proofs
findings.summary_md: This early news write-up reports that Ruby patched seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression engine and string case conversion and released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14. It describes a one-byte heap overflow and an integer overflow in case conversion, a double free during regular expression compilation and an out-of-bounds read in case-insensitive matching. The article notes that CVE identifiers were requested but not assigned and repeats the maintainers' proof-of-concept warning.
